issue.title: [copp] The calculation of rx_pps doesn't consider the factor of CBS

failure.body:
**Description**

We always failed the ARP,SNMP,SSH and IP2ME tests. The statistics are always greater than 660.
After analyzing the ARP receiving rate, I think if taking the CBS (600 packets) into consideration, it is reasonable why the average is always greater than 660.

1. In Figure 1, almost all the receiving rates are around 600, except the first second, 1180 packets are received in the first second.
Figure 1:
![rate_1](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/41297495/44373853-f9e57800-a51d-11e8-8e12-469736b94b7d.PNG)

2. In Figure 2, view the receiving rate by per 0.1 second in the first second.
Figure 2:
![rate_2](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/41297495/44373894-26998f80-a51e-11e8-88d5-3905b560ea33.PNG)

3. In this case 460 and 259 packets are received in the 1st and 2nd 0.1 second, they increase the **rx_pps** up to 86.41957 ((460+259)-600*0.2)/6.9313, 6.9313 is the **Test time**.

4. As CBS is up to 600 packets, I think the value of 460 and 259 packets at the beginning moment are still comply the configuration.

5. Since these tests (ARP, SNMP, SSH, and IP2ME) usually take less than 7 seconds, the CBS 600 makes a significant deviation on **rx_pps**.

resolution.title: [copp] skip packets in the first second for PolicyTest
resolution.description:
### Description of PR

Summary:
Fixes #685
Ignore the packets received in the first second because of CBS.

### Type of change

- [] Bug fix
- [x] Testbed and Framework(new/improvement)
- [] Test case(new/improvement)

### Approach
#### How did you do it?
Update copp_tests.py
-- add variable - needSlip to determine if need ignoring packets in the first second (PolicyTest)
-- add thread - slipSometime, flush dataplane after 1 second.

#### How did you verify/test it?
locally test.
Compare the statistics of **RX PPS**
#### Any platform specific information?
None
#### Supported testbed topology if it's a new test case?
N/A
